extracted.intended_audience: parties, attorneys, and judges involved in revocation and appeal proceedings before the Patent Court of Korea
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evidentiary rules and practice directions for filing, managing, hearing, and adjudicating revocation actions (and related appellate practice) in the Patent Court of Korea, including required content of petitions/briefs, evidence handling, hearings, experts, and document preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plaintiff petition contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The plaintiff shall set forth in detail the following matters in its petition: procedural background on KIPO and IPTAB examination/trial; a summary of the decision (arguments of the parties and judgment by IPTAB at trial stage); acknowledged parts and unacknowledged parts among the grounds for the decision; all arguments relating to erroneous grounds of the decision; notice of related cases (inclusive of progress and outcome of related trials and cancellation of decision actions including correction trials and petitions for correction, related civil cases on merits and petition cases, and criminal cases); and opinion on the overall litigation proceedings, including any plan for request for evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit evidence corresponding to each listed item and explanatory documents describing the purport of the evidence; include basic evidentiary documents and attachments such as power of attorney, corporate registry or certificate of corporate nationality (for foreign corp), and certificate of service of a decision. If these requisite matters or documents are omitted, the presiding judge or authorized court clerk will order supplementation (see supplemental submission rule and 3-week deadline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required evidentiary attachments for different revocation types
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific evidentiary documents are required by type of revocation case: for revocation of refusal decision cases: decision, application, preliminary rejection, amendment, opinion, rejection decision; for revocation of invalidation decision cases: decision, original register, registration publication, evidence relating to prior art (including prior conception, prior-registered trademarks, prior-used trademarks, prior designs); for revocation of decision on scope of right cases: decision, original register, registration publication, explanatory documents and drawings of invention (including conception, trademark, design, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully ensure these basic evidentiary documents and required attachments are included to avoid orders for supplementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental submission order and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition omits requisite matters or required basic evidentiary documents/attachments, the presiding judge or authorized court clerk issues an order to submit a supplemental brief or the omitted documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plaintiff must comply no later than 3 weeks after receipt of the order by submitting the preparatory brief, evidence, or documents as ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant response brief contents
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than 3 weeks from service of the plaintiff’s petition or brief containing specific grounds, the defendant shall submit a response brief including: response to the purport of petition; acknowledged/unacknowledged parts among plaintiff’s arguments; detailed rebuttal on unacknowledged parts; all additional arguments relating to proper grounds of the decision; notice of related cases (progress and outcome of related trials and revocation actions, civil cases, preliminary injunctions, criminal cases); statement on evidentiary documents submitted by the plaintiff; and opinion on overall litigation proceedings including plan for request for evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit cited evidence and explanatory documents for evidence together with the response brief; failure to comply may trigger a preparatory order requiring additional submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court may order additional rebuttal or evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding judge may issue an order requesting a party to submit detailed rebuttal arguments, additional evidence, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such an order issues, the recipient must submit the requested materials no later than 3 weeks after receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case classification after written arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of written arguments, the presiding judge reviews briefs and evidence and classifies the case as either (i) a case requiring immediate designation of a hearing or (ii) a case requiring a case management conference and preparatory hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification determines whether immediate hearing scheduling or further case management/preparatory steps are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparatory order for hearing: summary briefs and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: For cases requiring immediate designation of a hearing, the presiding judge may issue a preparatory order requesting summary briefs on disputed issues, and may designate deadlines for submission of arguments and evidence and for requests for evidence requiring substantial time (e.g., expert witnesses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow preparatory order deadlines closely; summary briefs should concentrate on disputed issues to conduct proceedings diligently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video conference for case management and topics
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding judge may discuss procedural matters via video/audio communication (video conference for case management). Items that may be discussed include: number and dates of hearings and matters for each hearing; deadlines for submission of arguments and evidence (including comprehensive briefs and expert statements, and number/volume of briefs); whether to request evidence requiring substantial time (verification, appraisal, expert witness) and deadline for such requests; whether to designate a technical advisor; whether to hold a technical explanatory session by the parties; whether to hold a claim construction hearing first; and confirmation and summary of issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court may notify parties of the video conference and issue a preparatory (scheduling) order based on the conference results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines for comprehensive briefs after video conference
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Court orders comprehensive briefs, the plaintiff shall submit a comprehensive brief no later than 3 weeks from the date of the video conference (or a deadline designated in the preparatory order), and the defendant shall submit a comprehensive brief no later than 3 weeks from the plaintiff’s submission (or other designated deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to these timelines unless the preparatory order specifies otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late submission of new or modified arguments and justifiable cause
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party seeks to add or modify an argument or submit evidence after the deadline designated in the preparatory order, the party must provide an explanation for failure to submit within the designated period based on a justifiable cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of justifiable cause: addition/modification of arguments related to statement of claim or defense; arguments that change the closest prior art for novelty/inventive step/free-to-practice defense; arguments adding/changing prior art and their combination relationships; arguments for lack of sufficient description based on a different legal provision, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparatory hearing purpose and late submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may hold a preparatory hearing to discuss preparatory matters, examine evidence, or hold a technical explanatory session. If a party seeks to add/modify an argument or submit evidence after closing of the preparatory hearing, the party must explain the failure to submit before closing based on a justifiable cause (similar to above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparatory hearing establishes the record and scope for later submissions — late additions require justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing conduct: time limits and order
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party shall present an oral argument for no longer than 20 minutes, in order of plaintiff then defendant. Even with multiple attorneys-of-record, the party’s oral arguments must be within the time period. The presiding judge may adjust time if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage oral presentations to fit 20-minute limit; seek court adjustment only if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadline for materials for oral arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any materials and summary briefs on disputed issues for oral arguments shall be submitted no later than 1 week before the designated date for each hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late submission may not be accepted; plan to file demonstrative materials in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrations and multimedia during hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: At hearings, parties may present oral arguments by bringing and demonstrating products related to the case (e.g., products implementing a registered patent/design, a prior art, an invention/design subject to confirmation), or by playing video materials or presenting photos via computer, visual presenter, etc., which might be helpful in understanding related technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare physical exhibits and multimedia and ensure compatibility with court presentation equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate oral hearings by issue
rubrics_metrics.description: If necessary, the Court may hold separate oral hearings according to specific issues when several issues are in dispute (examples: claim construction or whether prior art was published must be resolved first; multiple grounds for invalidation asserted; whether an invention subject to confirmation is specified and implemented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope of each hearing is limited to the designated disputed issue. After a hearing, the Court may disclose opinions (oral/written) on examined issues and order preparation for remaining issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction hearings and required notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claim construction is disputed and affects remaining issues, the presiding judge may conduct a claim construction hearing upon consultation with the parties. If there are pending correction trials or petitions for correction relating to disputed claims, parties must notify the Court of their progress and detailed plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court may disclose its opinion on claim construction (oral or written) and order parties to prepare for hearings on remaining issues based on that opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent handling of infringement actions and revocation actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If both a revocation action and an infringement action involving the same patent/utility model/trademark/design are pending before the Court and litigated by the same parties and attorneys, the Court may examine both actions in parallel and may organize preparatory proceedings for the actions in parallel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should be prepared for coordinated proceedings on related actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to adduce evidence: required statement of purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party files evidentiary documents or requests witness, inquiry of facts, certified copy, document submission order, verification, appraisal, etc., the party must specify in detail what the party intends to prove by the evidentiary means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that omit the specific intended evidentiary purpose may be deficient; be precise about the facts/issues the evidence will prove.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court preparatory proceeding for evidence examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If deemed necessary, the presiding judge may conduct a preparatory proceeding to discuss evidence examination procedure; procedural matters may be discussed via video conference upon consultation with the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ready to discuss timing, scope, and methods for evidence examination in a preparatory setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and appraisal procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If necessary, the Court may conduct verification or appraisal procedures either upon party request or ex officio. The Court may hold a preparatory proceeding to decide on the request, confirm objects and method of verification/appraisal, confirm factual premises, provide necessary materials, and select an appraiser. The Court may also order submission of objects for verification/appraisal if reason exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for verification/appraisal should specify objects, methods, and reasons; expect the Court to set procedures and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert witness requirements and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A party requesting an expert witness must attach a basic declaration confirming the expertise and objectivity of the witness. If the request is accepted, the party must submit a witness statement containing the testimony and a questionnaire for witness examination. Direct examination shall be within the scope of the statement; materials presented or cited in direct examination must be submitted as evidence before the date designated for examining the witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with declaration, statement, and documentary submission requirements; anticipate scope limits on direct examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreter and notification requirement for foreign expert witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: If an expert witness is a foreigner, parties may be accompanied by an interpreter for direct and cross-examinations. Parties must notify the Court of personal information and interpretation fees in advance. If a party cannot be accompanied by an interpreter, the party shall notify the Court 4 weeks before the witness examination date and file a request for designation of an interpreter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for interpreter logistics well in advance (4 weeks) including fees and personal data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparatory order for expert examination logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding judge may issue a preparatory order for examination of an expert witness including deadlines for submission of the expert’s statement and questionnaire, limitation of time for examination, and deadlines for submission of arguments/evidence for impeaching credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and comply with time limits and procedural deadlines set by the Court for expert evidence and impeachment materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical advisor designation and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: If deemed necessary, the Court may hear parties’ opinions and designate one or more technical advisors. A preparatory hearing may be held to help technical advisors understand the case. In hearings/preparatory hearings, technical advisors may directly question the parties with presiding judge approval. If a party must supplement its answer to a technical advisor’s question, the party shall submit its opinion in writing by a deadline designated by the presiding judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to address technical advisors and to provide written supplements to answers if ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document formatting: paper size, margins, font, and line spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper size of documents shall be A4 (210 mm x 297 mm) with a top margin of 45 mm, left and right margins of 20 mm, and a bottom margin of 30 mm (excluding page numbering). The font size shall be 12pt, and there shall be a line space of no less than 200% or 1.5 lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonconforming documents may be returned or require resubmission; adhere strictly to formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief length limit and repetition prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: The length of briefs shall not exceed 30 pages. If a brief of more than 30 pages is submitted, the presiding judge may return the brief and order resubmission reduced to 30 pages or less. In briefs, contents identical or similar to those included in petitions, responses or previous briefs shall not be needlessly repeated, nor cited in part or as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with the Court on brief length where necessary; avoid needless repetition to stay within page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence numbering and identification on briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: If any evidence supporting an argument is submitted, a number for the evidence shall be indicated on the corresponding portion thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly reference evidence numbers in the text where the evidence is relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical term definitions and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical terms shall be defined in footnotes and the sources thereof shall be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise definitions and citations for technical terminology to assist the Court and opposing parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary briefs and comprehensive briefs content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary briefs on disputed issues shall briefly state a summary of grounds for the petition for cancellation, undisputed facts, a summary table of disputed issues, explanation of evidence, additional evidence to be submitted, acceptance/denial of evidentiary documents, clarification, opinion on litigation proceedings, etc. Comprehensive briefs shall include a summary of all arguments regarding issues the Court ordered and main evidence for such arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure summary and comprehensive briefs to directly address Court-ordered issues and include main supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructive note: amendments/corrections to claims or descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: If any claims or descriptions in the specification of a patent or utility model are changed due to a petition for amendment or correction, such changes shall be stated in detail, and claims or descriptions in the specification subject to litigation shall be specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly identify amended text and the precise scope of what is litigated after amendment/correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructive note: changes in rights ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: If any rights relating to a patent, utility model, trademark or design at issue are changed, the details of such change and the ultimate holder of such rights shall be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentary proof of any transfer or change in rights and identify the current rights holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art inclusion/exclusion and role labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Among prior arts submitted at the trial phase, those included in and excluded from the revocation action shall be stated separately. It shall be clearly specified whether an evidentiary material is submitted either as a prior art or evidence for proving well-known technologies, ordinary skill in the art, level of ordinary skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ambiguity by labeling the role of each prior art/evidence and specifying which invention in a multi-invention document is being relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature comparison chart for prior art analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The features of prior arts shall be specified in detail, and a feature comparison chart comparing the corresponding features of the patented invention and each of the prior arts shall be submitted. The comparable features of well-known technologies shall also be specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear side-by-side comparisons to facilitate novelty/inventive step analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of person of ordinary skill in the art
rubrics_metrics.description: If an argument is made regarding inventive step or free-to-practice technology, the person of ordinary skill in the art and the level of ordinary skill in the art shall be specified in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define qualifications, experience, and knowledge level for the hypothetical PHOSITA used in the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arguments based on combination of prior arts
rubrics_metrics.description: If an argument is made regarding denial of inventive step by a combination of prior arts, a main prior art shall be selected, and a specific combination relationship of the prior arts and the grounds for the ease in combining the prior arts shall be specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the main prior art, how other prior arts are combined with it, and why a person of ordinary skill would have been motivated to combine them (example structure provided in guideline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description deficiency arguments and legal citations
rubrics_metrics.description: An argument regarding a lack of written description in the specification shall specify an applicable legal provision on which the argument is based (e.g., whether the patent can be readily practiced by the explanation therein — Article 42(3)1 of the Patent Act; whether a claim is supported by the explanation — Article 42(4)1; whether the scope of a claim is clearly specified — Article 42(4)2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the specific legal provision and explain how the specification fails that statutory requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for requesting a claim construction hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is necessary to conduct a hearing for claim construction first, the grounds shall be specified, and the terms for which claim construction is necessary, the descriptions relating to such terms in the specification, the parties’ proposed claim constructions, and specific grounds for such constructions shall be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise claim terms, textual support in the specification, and reasons why construction affects remaining issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation action against examiner’s rejection: defendant obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of a revocation action against a trial decision regarding examiner’s rejection, the defendant shall state the grounds for rejection set forth in a preliminary rejection notice and a rejection decision issued by an examiner of KIPO, and a preliminary rejection notice and a rejection decision issued by IPTAB, and clearly specify which of the rejection grounds are asserted in the litigation proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and document the exact rejection grounds relied upon from the administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory documents for evidence: purport and labelling
rubrics_metrics.description: All evidence submitted by a party shall be stated and the purport to be proved therefrom shall be briefly described. If evidence is submitted in relation to arguments regarding novelty, inventive step, or free-to-practice technology, it shall be clearly specified whether the evidence is submitted as a prior art or as evidence of a well-known technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each evidentiary item should include a short explanatory note linking it to the legal/factual issue it supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary document formalities and translation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if material was submitted during examination or trial, it may not serve as a basis for judgment unless submitted as evidence during litigation. Written documents in a foreign language shall be submitted with a translation attached (machine translations shall not be submitted). Particularly for main evidence such as prior arts, full-text translations, not excerpts, shall be submitted. In translations, portions concerning evidentiary purport shall be highlighted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide certified human translations of full documents and highlight the evidentiary-relevant passages; ensure duplication between parties’ submissions is minimized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary document titling, single-item rule, numbering and color requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An evidentiary document shall indicate a title if it exists, or a summary if it has no title. Each evidentiary document shall contain only a single evidentiary item; if items are related, use multi-level numbering (e.g., Plaintiff’s Exhibit No. 2-1, 2-2). For avoidance of confusion, numbering of prior arts submitted at trial stage shall be followed when submitting new prior arts in the revocation action. If there is any product, model, photograph, video material etc. that may facilitate understanding, parties shall submit the same as evidence. For trademarks/designs, if the original is in color, the evidentiary document shall be submitted in color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow single-item-per-document rule, use clear numbering schemes that continue prior numbering, and submit color originals where required.
